task.name: A project cannot extend a sandbox capability preset, so a toolchain need the shipped presets do not anticipate has no configuration path
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A project whose gate requires the host Apple toolchain cannot build or test its
real app target under the sandbox, even with `sandbox.capability_profile: xcode`
selected and applied. The capability gap does not surface as a capability error —
it reaches the operator as a code-quality verdict.

In `hdp` run `70462a5b72a0`, story #248 ran three dev iterations, cost $10.03,
and ended `REQUEST_CHANGES`. Both blocking findings were the same objection
restated: the watch target was never built or exercised.

```
[P1] … A regression in the real watch alarm flow … would currently reach users
     without a failing test, because this change only exercised the pure
     scheduling helper …
[P1] … The watch alarm refactor still reached review without a successful
     app-scheme build, so the new watch-path source was only exercised through
     iOS unit tests and not through the real thebos target that embeds HDPWatch
```

The reviewer was correct on both counts. The dev agent could not comply, because
its own logs record three separate denials:

```
xcodebuild verification was blocked by sandbox constraints: CoreSimulator…
xcodebuild test` was blocked by a power-assertion denial
xcodebuild` cannot use CoreSimulator here, and package resolution cann[ot]…
```

The profile was in effect throughout — every dev invocation logs
`sandbox capability profile: xcode (6 extra write roots, 4 mach services)`.
The story was recorded as `review_rejected`, and the sprint's own NEXT advice was
to address the review findings and re-run, which would spend another cycle on a
finding no amount of dev work can resolve.

## Expected behavior

When a project declares that its gate depends on host toolchain capabilities, the
sandbox should either grant what that toolchain actually requires or fail the run
with an explicit capability error naming what was denied. A capability gap should
never reach the operator disguised as a code-quality verdict, because that routes
them toward more dev cycles against a condition no dev work can satisfy. A project
should also be able to express capability requirements that the shipped presets do
not anticipate, rather than being limited to selecting one whole preset or none;
the set of things a real toolchain needs is not knowable in advance from inside
this repository.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** with `capability_profile: xcode` applied, dev cannot run
  `xcodebuild` against a real app target; the resulting unverifiable code is
  rejected by review and the story is classified `review_rejected` rather than as
  an environment failure.

- **Evidence:** `hdp` run `70462a5b72a0` — profile application logged at
  `run-70462a5b72a0.log:165` (`sandbox capability profile: xcode (6 extra write
  roots, 4 mach services)`); the three denial messages above appear in
  `.forge/logs/issues-248,245,246,231/issue-248/*.log`; final verdict
  `REQUEST_CHANGES` with both P1s quoted above, $10.03 across three iterations.
  Inspecting the preset directly: `preset_names()` returns `('xcode',)`, and
  `get_preset('xcode').mach_services` is
  `com.apple.CoreSimulator.CoreSimulatorService`,
  `com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd`, `com.apple.lsd.mapdb`,
  `com.apple.system.notification_center`.


- **Correction (supersedes the original confirmed cause):** an earlier revision
  of this issue attributed the package-resolution failure to the absence of a
  network-egress concept in the preset model. That is wrong. The dev agent's own
  handoff in run `5096bd4a46e3` records the failure occurring against
  already-resolved derived data with all five package checkouts present, and
  persisting under `-disableAutomaticPackageResolution
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -skipPackageUpdates`. Network was never
  reached. The failure is `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`: SwiftPM
  compiles package manifests by invoking `sandbox-exec`, and macOS refuses to
  apply a sandbox inside the `sandbox-exec` confinement forge already established.
  Apple's documented workaround for that collision,
  `defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDEPackageSupportDisableManifestSandbox`, is
  denied in turn because `~/Library/Preferences` is not a granted write root.

- **Confirmed cause:** two distinct defects were conflated here. The first is
  mechanical and not addressable by any grant: a toolchain that itself invokes
  `sandbox-exec` cannot run inside a `sandbox-exec` confinement, so no preset
  content and no extension to the preset model changes the outcome. That defect is
  tracked in #2050. What remains genuinely scoped to this issue is the capability
  model itself: `SandboxCapabilityPreset` carries only `name`, `description`,
  `supported_platforms`, `write_roots` and `mach_services`, and
  `config.types.SandboxConfig` exposes only `capability_profile: str | None`, so a
  project can select a whole preset but cannot add a write root, a mach service, or
  any other grant — and `xcode` remains the only preset. A project whose toolchain
  needs anything outside those grants has no configuration path, independently of
  the nesting collision.

- **Affected code path:** `config.sandbox_capabilities` —
  `SandboxCapabilityPreset`, `get_preset`, `preset_names`, `resolve_capabilities`;
  `config.types.SandboxConfig` (`config/types.py:614`) and
  `sandbox_capability_profile` (`config/types.py:258`).

- **Fix-success criterion:** a project can express a capability requirement the
  shipped presets do not anticipate — at minimum an additional write root and an
  additional mach service — without a code change in this repository, and a
  requirement that cannot be satisfied terminates the run with an explicit
  capability error naming what was denied.

## Notes

This issue has been narrowed. The two behaviors originally bundled here are now
tracked separately, because they have different causes and different fixes:

- #2050 — the dev agent cannot execute the project's declared toolchain. This is
  the nesting collision, and it is what actually blocks an Apple app-target build.
- #2051 — review blocks on agent-reported build evidence the run cannot produce
  while the coordinator holds its own gate result. This is the trust-ordering
  defect that turned the capability gap into a `review_rejected` verdict.
- #2029 — a capability gap is never surfaced as the actionable cause.

What remains here is the capability model: project-extensible grants. Whether the
model should also gain a network-egress concept is unresolved and, on the evidence
above, is not on the critical path for the observed failures — package resolution
failed with the cache fully populated and the network never reached.

[ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-dev-phase-verification-capability.md) (Accepted 2026-07-29) owns the dev-phase
verification decision and records this issue as its **option C**: making the
capability model project-extensible is worth doing on its own merits but is
explicitly *not* the hdp unblock, because the nesting collision is not an
allowlist problem. No ADR owns the capability model itself.

`docs/adr/0004-execution-substrate.md` §9 records this ceiling as field evidence.
Its characterisation of the SwiftPM denial as a network-egress limitation carried
the same error corrected above and **has now been amended** (commit `c9ec55c`);
the §9 verdict is unaffected.

handoff.summary: Made the sandbox capability model project-extensible. SandboxConfig now carries additive write_roots and mach_services next to capability_profile; config/load.py parses and validates them (rejecting malformed shapes) while still refusing allow_default/disabled/mode. resolve_capabilities gained keyword-only write_roots/mach_services parameters (empty defaults, so existing callers in audit.py/audit_storage.py/dev_phase.py are unchanged) that merge project grants with the selected preset, de-duplicate after ~ expansion, retain project provenance, and fail closed: a grant resolving to / or the invoking home is refused naming the path, and a mach service on a non-Darwin backend is refused naming the services. dev_phase stamps the declarations onto the dev ModelProfile and audits the merged set (plus requested values and unsupported_reason when refused); runner_claude and runner_gemini pass them into workspace_effect_sandbox_command, which merges them into the Seatbelt/bwrap profile with deny-default intact. Per the plan reviewer's P1, transports that cannot express a declaration (codex, gh-aw, API, and the API fallback from a declaring CLI profile) now refuse before dispatch with the existing SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED marker instead of silently dropping the grants. Docs updated in docs/guides/inputs-reference.md and the sandbox_capabilities module docstring.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A project can express a capability requirement the shipped presets do not anticipate — at minimum an additional write root and an additional mach service — without a code change in this repository.
acceptance_criteria.notes: sandbox.write_roots / sandbox.mach_services in forge.yaml, additive to any selected preset and usable with no preset at all. Covered by test_config_load.py (load), test_sandbox_capabilities.py (merge, dedup, inline-only, real sandbox-exec acceptance), and test_coord_sandbox_capabilities.py (config -> runner profile -> audit seam).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A requirement that cannot be satisfied terminates the run with an explicit capability error naming what was denied.
acceptance_criteria.notes: UnsupportedCapabilityProfileError names the denied write root (filesystem/home root) and names the requested mach services on a non-Darwin backend; the runner's pre-existing fail-closed path returns SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED. Extended to transports that cannot express a declaration at all (codex/ghaw/API/API-fallback), which now refuse before dispatch. Audit records zero grants plus requested_profile/requested_write_roots/requested_mach_services and unsupported_reason.

story_deviations: The audit payload's project_write_roots/project_mach_services keys are emitted only when the project actually declared grants. This keeps the record's base shape byte-identical for every run that declares nothing, so no CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION bump / MIGRATION_HELPERS entry is implied for a purely additive field. Flagging it because the payload docstring previously promised 'always emits every key'; that promise still holds for the applied set.

Scope beyond the plan's Step 3, following the plan reviewer's P1: added runners/sandbox.capability_transport_refusal() and wired it into runners/cli.py so codex, gh-aw, API, and the API-fallback path fail closed. Without this the audit could claim grants the actual runner never received.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 misses supported dev-runner callers. dev_phase.py stamps the project sandbox declarations onto every dev ModelProfile, but runner_codex.py uses Codex's native --sandbox mode and never calls workspace_effect_sandbox_command, while API dev profiles execute tools through runners/api.py and tool_runtime.py. Those paths would neither apply the declared roots/services nor emit SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED. API fallback from a CLI profile can also enter the ignored path. The audit could therefore claim grants that the actual runner never received.
  Suggestion: Enumerate every supported dev transport. Apply the declarations where its sandbox API can express them; otherwise reject the invocation before dispatch with a capability error naming the requested write roots and mach services. Add Codex, API, and API-fallback seam tests proving either application or explicit fail-closed behavior.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Stated risk 1 (mach-service satisfiability unprovable without host probing) is retired by Step 2's non-Darwin fail-closed rule plus the Step 4 Linux-denial test, and stated risk 2 (ModelProfile field additions breaking direct constructions) is retired by empty-tuple defaults plus the Step 4 runner-wrapper tests — recorded here so both are visibly resolved rather than dropped. Neither blocks.
  Suggestion: No action needed; keep the Linux mach-service denial test in Step 4 so the fail-closed boundary stays enforced.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 only updates docs/guides/inputs-reference.md, but two other places assert the now-obsolete contract: the module docstring in src/theforge/config/sandbox_capabilities.py ('A project cannot author, extend, or override the contents of one') and the forge.yaml example comment at inputs-reference.md:986.
  Suggestion: Amend the sandbox_capabilities.py module docstring to state that presets stay forge-owned but projects may add bounded additive grants, and update the inputs-reference.md:986 example alongside the §'Sandbox capability profiles' section at line 1161.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 does not name coordinator/audit.py:540,774 or coordinator/audit_storage.py:1266-1269, which call resolve_capabilities(None).audit_payload() as a default. These stay correct only if the new grant parameters are keyword-only with empty defaults.
  Suggestion: Add the merge inputs to resolve_capabilities as keyword-only parameters defaulting to empty tuples so existing positional callers (dev_phase.py:872, sandbox.py:482, audit.py, audit_storage.py) are unchanged.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
